profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at CNN | Former TV news producer turned web developer | Empowering young women of color to explore careers in tech
profile.summary:
Sydney is a Senior Software Developer at CNN with over five years of experience. Originally a television news producer, she discovered a passion for code and left broadcasting for a career in web development. Her journey came full circle when she returned to CNN to build web applications for the same teams she once covered elections with.

Sydney is passionate about tech and hopes to inspire young women of color to pursue careers in the industry. When she’s not coding, you can catch her volunteering with Black Girls Code as a Tech Assistant. She is also apart of the leadership team for Women Who Code and has been featured as a panelist for the organization . She is a familiar face around local tech meet-ups,  but if you don’t find her there, she is probably chasing her two sons.

Intensive knowledge in: Javascript, React, Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Docker and RESTful APIs.

projects.title: Show Me The Money, Full Stack Javascript Application
projects.description: Show Me The Money is a full-stack personal finance app where users can buy courses to take their finances to the next level. This app was built in the MEAN stack using MongoDB, Express.js, AngularJS and Node.js.  A user can view all the available courses, get in-depth look into each course and add or delete a course or courses to or from his or her cart. Used D3.js for datamap of the average credit card debt in the United States.

projects.title: outFttr, Full Stack Javascript Application
projects.description: outFttr is a wardrobe planner and closet organizer app that lets a user easily create their own digital closet and plan their outfits ahead of time. I lead a team of four developers in creating a full stack application built with Node.js, MongoDB and Express.js. We used the AWS module to add photos to items and OpenWeatherMap weather API for weather updates on our app.

organizations.name: Women Who Code
organizations.description: Women Who Code is a global non-profit dedicated to inspiring women to excel in technology careers. It aims to provide an avenue into tech, empowering women with skills needed for professional advancement, and providing environments where networking and mentorship are valued.

organizations.name: National Association of Black Journalists
organizations.description: The National Association of Black Journalists (NABJ) is an organization of journalists, students and media-related professionals that provides quality programs and services to and advocates on behalf of black journalists worldwide.
